text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Lebanon set to be blamed for Katyusha rocket strike. Ceasefire monitors clash as violence in south continues.
- President Hrawi tries to steer nation out of danger.
- Amnesty team visits south to study abuses of human rights.
- Questions over identification of Jerusalem bombers.
- Katyusha attacks wound more civilians in south.
- Lebanon renews invitation for Iraqi trade visit.
- Israeli operations reach Janta in Bekaa Valley and rocket hits orphanage.
- Prime Minister Hariri meets Syrian President Assad.
- Parliament Speaker Berri at tobacco festival: There will be no widescale Israeli military operation.
- Foreign Minister Bouez: Arafat is working for Israel and justifying its attacks against Lebanon.
